import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length9_98/training_9.csv"
]

# Read all source files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = [pd.read_csv(f, index_col=0) for f in source_files]

# Concatenate all DataFrames (UNION operation)
df_union = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Ensure the schema and types match the target schema
df_union = df_union.astype({
    'admit': 'int64',
    'gre': 'int64',
    'gpa': 'float64',
    'prestige': 'int64'
})

# Write the final DataFrame to the target CSV file
df_union.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_98/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
